Anthropic warns it may soon cross its own threshold for faster AI progress

• Anthropic's new filing warns it may soon meet its own threshold for accelerated progress, though no current model crosses it.
• The New York Times and three other papers sued Brave, alleging it scraped their articles and sold access to AI companies.
• Gemini reads your Gmail to summarise and draft replies, and Google says it does not train its foundational AI models on personal emails.

items.hook: Anthropic tells investors its AI may soon speed up its own progress[S1].
items.text:
Anthropic tells investors its AI may soon speed up its own progress.

• The warning sits in the Risk Factors of Anthropic's revised S-1A filing.
• It says capabilities may advance faster than its safety, alignment and security measures.
• Anthropic says it has missed such jumps before, and no current model crosses the line.

Our read: When the builder itself warns that safety may lag, the debate about AI speed stops being theory.

Your take: Should AI labs slow down when safety lags? Tell us in the comments.

items.hook: Gemini can read your Gmail, and many of its features are on by default[S4].
items.text:
Gemini can read your Gmail, and many of its features are on by default.

• Gemini summarises recent emails, creates to-do lists and drafts replies.
• Google says it does not train Gemini on your personal emails.
• Google says Gemini does not hold onto your data after each request.

Do this: Open your Gmail settings and check which Gemini features are switched on.

Your take: Do you let AI read your work email? Tell us in the comments.

items.hook: The New York Times sues Brave, saying it sold scraped news to AI firms[S3].
items.text:
The New York Times sues Brave, saying it sold scraped news to AI firms.

• The suit says Brave indexed more than 30 billion web pages with an unidentified crawler.
• Named customers include Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere.
• Three more papers filed a similar lawsuit the same day in Manhattan.

Our read: The copyright fight is moving from AI labs to the companies that supply their data.

Your take: Should AI companies pay for the news they use? Tell us in the comments.
